Step 42: forwards, the pictures read as fade-out-and-reappear. At the end it clears fades and puts back the view's ghost (player.js:919-920). publish.py strips only review and text_key (AUTHORING_KEYS, line 61), so the website copy keeps reappear and will play the fade.

verdict.reason: I checked this and could not refute it. The Step 22c pictures were saved at 13:22, after steps.json was written at 13:16, so they show the current guide. In r5_w760, r5_w1000 and r5_w1920_Step22c.png the close-up is almost all a flat brown band, the VCC wire, with the green GND wire curving across the top. So 22c is the only one that fails. The cause is where G11 is: its target, [653.61, 887.97, 1310.94], is 2.5 mm from V11's, and the brown wire put on V11 in Step 21 rises between the camera and G11. verdict.reason: Confirmed. In player/js/placed() the camera itself moves: both the target and the camera move by `by` = shift x radius (0.7 x 150.5 = about 105 mm along dir x up), and the camera keeps its direction. This is not a pan of the picture. The model is now seen from a different place, so the parallax and what is hidden change. The pictures show it plainly. In before_title_1440x900.png the right (H2) side face is wide, about x 760-870, and H2's label is at about (845,555). H11's label and the cable loop behind H14 are visible, and the keys are seen at a steep slant. In r5_title_1440x900.png the H2 side is close to edge-on, a sliver at about x 1080-1135 with its label squeezed. H11 and the loop are hidden. The keys and the 4-digit display are seen much more face-on, so the H9 labels can now be read. The before picture's model sat left of the middle, so the old framing was already shifted the other way. The total sideways change in camera position is therefore about one radius or more, which fits the reviewer's 11-15 degree estimate at a distance of about 400-450 mm. The README (LEE'S FIFTH ROUND, first bullet, lines 261-264) and the guide.py comment at line 1225 describe only a move to the right at "the same size". They do not mention that the title picture is now seen from a different angle than the view pinned in round 2. Lee asked only for the model to be moved right. The new look may be acceptable or even better, but it is a visible change Lee should be told about. Nothing here harms a student.

findings.where: PMG README.txt:272-273; CLAUDE.md:83; docs/cadasio-patterns.md:389 (against the rulebook's own lines 79 and 427); r5_w1000_fwd42c_0450.png and 0500.png
findings.title: The docs call the Step 42 fade the same as the published guides' cross-fade, but it fades out fully before fading in
findings.evidence: The rulebook says the published guides move wired things by cross-fading complete copies (line 79: 'complete copies (part + its routed wires) cross-fade'; line 427). The README ('The published guides move wired things so too'), CLAUDE.md and the new rulebook row present this as the same. The player instead fades everything out over 0.8 s, then in over 0.8 s (player.js:860). In between (fwd42c_0450-0550) the module and every wire are gone. The dot matrix and the 4-digit display lie on the bench with bare caps and nothing plugged in, which could briefly read as 'unplugged' to a student. This is not against Lee's wording ('fade and reappear'), but the docs' claim does not match what plays.
findings.suggestion: Reword the three docs to say it fades out, then in, unlike Cadasio's simultaneous cross-fade. Offer Lee the overlapping cross-fade as an alternative to try if the empty moment looks odd.

verdict.reason:
The finding's facts hold, but the docs already describe the motion accurately, so this is not a real defect.

What the finding gets right: player/js/player.js:860 holds the motion at its start for the first FADE_MS while the parts fade out, then at its end for the second FADE_MS while they fade in. One copy is gone before the other appears. r5_w1000_fwd42c_0500.png shows the bench at the halfway point: the module, the USB A end and every wire are gone, and the dot matrix and 4-digit display are left with bare caps (0300 still shows them part-faded). Cadasio's swap is different: one overlapping 800 ms cross-fade (evidence doc line 853, "in one 800 ms step").

Why it is not real:
1. All three docs say it happens in sequence. README 272-273: "fade out where they lie on the bench (one beat, 0.8 s) and fade in where the step leaves them ... (a beat)". CLAUDE.md 83: "fade out where they are and fade in where they end, a beat each". Rulebook 389: "fades out where it lies and fades in where it is held". No reader of these lines would expect one overlapping cross-fade.
2. The phrase "as the published guides move wired things (section 4)" is about the kind of move: a swap of whole copies instead of tweening wired things along a path. That is what rulebook line 79 contrasts ("moved by swapping poses ... They are tweened only before any wire constrains them"). The comparison is loose about timing, but the docs do not claim the same timing.
3. Lee asked for a "fade and reappear in final position transition ... and see how that looks". Fading out and then fading in is the literal reading of that. The moment with nothing plugged in is part of the look Lee asked to judge, not a departure from it.
4. A student sees none of these docs. On screen the step's caption names everything that moves, and the empty moment lasts well under a second inside a 1.6 s transition Lee is about to review.

At most this is a wording nicety in internal docs. Offering Lee an overlapping cross-fade is a reasonable follow-up idea, but it is not a defect.

Without `reappear` the code behaves exactly as before: `ec = e` (858), `shown` stays null (891), `faded` is unchanged (917), and km/e are computed as before.

findings.where: player/js/player.js:841-842 (same() / parts), with composePose 69-80 and mixPose 57-66
findings.title: 'Changes place' is decided by comparing JSON text, so parts that stay put still fade
findings.evidence: parts = keys(end) where JSON.stringify(start) !== JSON.stringify(end). `start` is the live pose from the previous frame. For a rider on a turned carrier, composePose builds that pose in the player: full-precision floats with `at` = the part's bounding-sphere centre. It can never match steps.json's 2-decimal pose. Step 42: the dot matrix caps NAUO134-138 and the 4-digit display caps NAUO259-262 ride with pose [0,0,0] on NAUO81 and NAUO79 (both turned 40 deg). Their offsets are identical in 42 and 42c, yet they are selected and faded. In r5_w1000_fwd42c_0300/0450/0550 the dot matrix caps go see-through, then pale; at _0500 its header pins stand bare. On the 4-digit display the cap edge lines vanish mid-way. The 12 button caps at the other ends of the same faded wires (NAUO86-93, CAP_GND1-4) ride on carriers with no offset, so composePose returns the steps.json pose itself and they stay solid. So whether a part fades depends on how its pose was computed, not on whether it moves. Any part with a turned offset at rest would also be caught: mixPose(a, a, 1) rebuilds the axis and angle from a quaternion, e.g. 0.57735 becomes 0.5773502691896258. A kit that turns parts on the bench would fade stationary parts on any `reappear` step. Neither the code comment ('those whose pose differs') nor the README's 'the module with all it carries' describes this.
findings.suggestion: Compare where the two poses put the part instead of their text, as runthrough.js does. Map the part's sphere centre and an offset point through stage.poseMatrix(start) and stage.poseMatrix(end), and count the part as moved if either point shifts by more than about 0.05 mm. Do not use poseGap(): it ignores `at`, and composePose writes a different pivot than steps.json, so it would still mismatch. If the display caps should fade with their wires, say so (e.g. add riders whose wires fade) and make the button caps match.

verdict.reason:
The code path is as described, but in this guide its only visible effect is harmless, so the finding does not hold up as a defect.

What I confirmed:
- player/js/player.js:841-842 picks the parts to fade by comparing JSON text. `start[id]` comes from the previous frame's `liveOffsets` (line 759). In steps.json, Step 42 and Step 42c (views 84/85) give the nine caps NAUO134-138 and NAUO259-262 the carry pose [0,0,0] on NAUO81 and NAUO79, and both carriers are turned 40 deg. For those caps, composePose (lines 69-80) builds a pose with full-precision floats and `at` set to the sphere centre, so the text never matches steps.json and the nine caps are faded even though they do not move.
- NAUO81 and NAUO79 themselves ride on NAUO63, which has no offset, so composePose returns the steps.json pose unchanged and they stay solid.
- The pictures match this: r5_w1000_fwd42c_0300 shows the dot matrix caps pale, and _0500 shows its header pins bare.

Why it does not matter here:
- Each of the nine affected caps is the display-side end of a wire that ends on the I/O module. The module moves (NAUO78, NANO and the others differ between 42 and 42c), so every one of those wires fades anyway.
- What a student sees is each whole jumper wire, cap included, fading out and back in. That fits Lee's request to fade the messy wiring and reappear in place. Nothing jumps, nothing ends up in the wrong place, and frame _1000 shows every cap back on its pin.
- The inconsistency with the button caps (NAUO86-93, CAP_GND1-4) cannot be seen in Step 42. The buttons sit inside the closed case and are not visible from the step's straight-behind camera (frames _0000 and _1000).
- No other parts are affected. Of the parts in Step 42 that are turned but do not move, only these nine caps are mis-selected. NAUO79 and NAUO81 compare equal.
- The wider claim (stationary turned parts in another kit would fade) is hypothetical. No other guide uses `reappear`.

This is fragile code worth hardening by comparing where the two poses put the part, not their text. It is not a defect a student or Lee would notice in this round.

findings.where: player/js/player.js:715 (turnAround only for `away`), 759 (start from liveOffsets), 870-879 (riders rebuilt from carry poses)
findings.title: Next or Prev during the 1.6 s fade brings back the tangle, or flashes the end state
findings.evidence: turnAround only covers deconstruction steps (`from.away` / `to.away`), and during the first 0.8 s liveOffsets still hold the bench poses (km = 0). (a) Next during that half: double-click, or holding ArrowRight (1237). go(43) starts NAUO78 from liveOffsets, the turned bench pose, because `was` is true (797-799). Step 43 moves the module (`moving: [NAUO78]`), so it slides from the bench up to H4 in one 0.8 s move. Its wires keep routes 156-177 (43.wires == 42c.wires), so they are not 'changing' and are drawn as the 42c routes stretched from H4 down to the moving module: the tangle Lee asked to hide. (b) Prev during that half: go() clears the fades, so everything snaps solid. The rider loop ignores `start` and places NAUO78 at throughPoses([42c carry pose, 42 carry pose], e = 0), the held position over H4. The A end NAUO283 likewise goes to its 42c spot. So the learner sees the 42c end state, solid with all its wires, then watches it fade out and back in at the bench. (c) Prev during the second half also snaps the partly faded parts to solid before fading them out again. Normal steps share the general interrupt behaviour, but on this step it undoes the reason for the fade, and the step is twice as long, so interruptions are more likely.
findings.suggestion: In go(), when the previous animation was a `reappear` still running: for the reverse step (prev.to === from && prev.src === to), treat it like turnAround (t0 = now - (dur - elapsed)). The fade curve is symmetric, so the opacity and the half carry over unchanged. For any other destination, finish it first (e.g. call stepAnimation(prev.t0 + prev.dur) before computing `start`), so the next step starts from the end poses, not the bench.

verdict.reason:
The code reading is correct, but this is how the player already handles any step that is interrupted. The reappear change does not introduce it, and makes this step less exposed to it than round 4 was.

What I confirmed in /Users/lee-johnson/Desktop/Claude_Cadasio/player/js/player.js:
- Next (line 1215) and ArrowRight (line 1237) call go() at once, with no guard while a step is still playing.
- turnAround (line 715) only applies to deconstruction steps (`away`).
- In the first half of the reappear (lines 859-860), km = e = 0, so liveOffsets keep the bench poses.
- (a) Next in that half: go(86) takes start[NAUO78] = liveOffsets, the turned bench pose (lines 757-760). In steps.json, Step 43 has no carry for NAUO78 and its offsets for NAUO78 are [0, 102.3, 0.2], the same as 42c's, and 43.wires equals 42c.wires (routes 156-177). So the module mixPoses from the bench to over H4 in 800 ms, solid (clearFades at line 754). The 42c routes are skinned to it (skinned(), lines 113-143) and the A end NAUO283 snaps. Confirmed.
- (b) Prev in that half: the rider loop (lines 869-878) uses `was` = the 42c carry pose with e = 0. So NAUO78 shows solid at the held pose and fades out, then fades in on the bench. Confirmed.
- (c) Prev in the second half: the partly faded parts pop to solid. Confirmed.

Why it does not count as a defect of this round:
1. Every build step behaves this way. Interrupting a step restarts from liveOffsets with no turn-around, and riders ignore `start`.
2. Round 4's Step 42 (HEAD steps.json: 42c carries 4 vias for NAUO78 and NAUO283, plus wire_via, so 5 beats, about 4 s) had the same artefacts:
   - A double-click early in its first beat also glided the module from near the bench to the held pose, with the held routes skinned.
   - Prev mid-step also jumped the rider to the held pose: the staged branch with back = true, then `was` = the 42c pose.
3. With reappear, the window where Next brings back the glide is the first 0.8 s only. Round 4's whole 4 s motion was exposed. Past 0.8 s, liveOffsets already hold the final poses and Next is clean.
4. It needs a second Next or Prev within 0.8 s. A brief solid glide or flash follows and the state then settles correctly. Lee's request ("see how that looks") is about the normal transition, which these changes implement.

The suggested fix (a reverse turn-around, or finishing the reappear before starting the next step) would be a nice robustness improvement. It is not a problem this change introduced, and it does not undermine what Lee asked for.

findings.title: Latent: a reappear step with ghosts, new parts or new riders would not fade them
findings.evidence: None of these arise on Step 42 (the visible sets match, no ghost, no fresh riders), but stepgen documents place(..., reappear=True) as a general option. (1) The ghost loop runs after the reappear fades and calls stage.setFade for every ghost id, guarded only by `anim.fade`. A ghost part that also changes place would have its fade overwritten (no fade out or in), and any ghost alpha jumps at half-way because e is forced to 0 or 1. Stored offsets are rounded. So a part that does not move can count as changed. Example: the dot matrix's five device-end caps (NAUO134-138) ride on NAUO81 at [0,0,0], and their 42 and 42c offsets are identical ({'t': [111.28, -29.98, 145.85], 'r': [0,0,1,40.0004], 'at': [537.09, 959.56, 1218.77]} for NAUO134). The button wires' far-end caps (riding on buttons at ZERO) compare equal and stay solid. Harmless in Step 42, because those wires fade anyway. But the documented rule is 'parts whose pose differs', and in another kit a still part with a turned pose would blink out and back.

NAUO79 and NAUO81 ride NAUO63 at ZERO, and composePose then returns the stored pose itself, so they compare equal and stay solid in 0500. verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this by reading the code and could not. In /Users/lee-johnson/Desktop/Claude_Cadasio/player/js/player.js:

- Nothing blocks a click while a step is still playing. Line 1215 is `$('next').onclick = () => go(cur + 1)`, line 1216 is the same for Prev, and line 1237 does the same for the arrow keys.
- For the first FADE_MS (800 ms) of a reappear animation, stepAnimation() sets km = e = 0 (line 860). So liveOffsets (line 863) holds the start poses. The riders get the same treatment through composePose and `was`, since paced(1) returns e = 0.
- steps.json, views 84-86: on Step 42 and 42c, NAUO78 (the I/O module) rides on NAUO63. Its pose is the bench pose on Step 42 (a 120° turn) and [0, 102.3, 0.2] on Step 42c. On Step 43 it is a hover view with moving = [NAUO78] and the same offset [0, 102.3, 0.2].

What happens if Next is pressed to reach Step 43 during the fade-out:
- go() clears the fades (line 753), so the faded parts and wires turn solid at once.
- was(NAUO78) is true, so start = liveOffsets, which is still the bench pose (line 759).
- The step is done-to-hover, so it gets no `ways`. The block at line 787 skips NAUO78 because it was already on screen.
- So stepAnimation() runs mixPose(bench, held, e) over 800 ms. The Nano, plug and caps follow it as riders. The wires stay tied to their ends by skinned(), so they stretch and bend with the module.

Prev in the first 800 ms of going back from Step 42c to Step 42 does the same in reverse. liveOffsets holds the pose over H4, and go(41c) (from a hover view, so no ways) glides the module from there to the bench.

The turnAround handling (line 715) covers only deconstruction (`away`) steps, not reappear. The README's fifth-round section describes only the uninterrupted fade ("going back, the same the other way"), not this case.

So a student who presses Next twice quickly (or holds the arrow key) sees the module and its wires pop solid and swing through each other: the motion Lee asked this step to replace. This only happens within 0.8 s of the previous press, so it is minor. The suggested fix (start from the reappear view's end poses when such an animation is cut short) fits the code.
